statement: The log determinant of an $n \times n$ matrix $A$ is the logarithm of its determinant, denoted $\log \det(A)$ (or $\log(\det(A))$).

symbols.meaning: matrix logarithm of A satisfying \exp(L) = A

properties.property: For a positive definite matrix $A$, $\operatorname{tr}\left(I - A^{-1}\right) \leq \log \det(A) \leq \operatorname{tr}(A - I)$, with equality if and only if $A = I$.
properties.why: follows from bounds given by the trace operator on positive definite matrices (derivable via Kullback–Leibler divergence between two multivariate normal distributions)

properties.property: For real matrices $A$, $\log(\det(\exp(A))) = \operatorname{tr}(A)$; equivalently, given any logarithm $L$ satisfying $\exp(L) = A$, $\det(A) = \exp(\operatorname{tr}(L))$.
properties.why: every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\exp(\lambda)$ of $\exp(A)$, with determinant equal to the product of eigenvalues and trace equal to their sum

assumptions.assumption: $A$ is a square matrix with strictly positive determinant, $\det(A) > 0$ (e.g., a positive definite matrix).
assumptions.breaks_when: $\det(A) \leq 0$, where the real logarithm is undefined.

assumptions.assumption: $A$ is invertible ($0$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$).
assumptions.breaks_when: $0$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, which implies $\det(A) = 0$.

failure_modes.signature: Real logarithm cannot be evaluated without complex logarithm extensions.
failure_modes.cause: $\det(A) < 0$, which occurs when the product of the eigenvalues of $A$ is negative.

failure_modes.signature: $A^{-1}$ does not exist, causing the lower bound $\operatorname{tr}(I - A^{-1})$ to fail.
failure_modes.cause: $A$ fails to be positive definite and has a zero eigenvalue.
